claim: Music can arouse feelings of euphoria and craving, similar to tangible rewards that involve the striatal dopaminergic system.
excerpt: Music, an abstract stimulus, can arouse feelings of euphoria and craving, similar to tangible rewards that involve the striatal dopaminergic system.

claim: In listeners, endogenous dopamine release was found in the striatum at peak emotional arousal during music listening.
excerpt: we found endogenous dopamine release in the striatum at peak emotional arousal during music listening.
context: PET scanning with [11C]raclopride in human listeners. Release at peak arousal is a measured association.

claim: In fMRI of the same listeners, the caudate was more involved during anticipation and the nucleus accumbens during the experience of peak emotional responses.
excerpt: the caudate was more involved during the anticipation and the nucleus accumbens was more involved during the experience of peak emotional responses to music.
context: fMRI with the same stimuli and listeners. 'More involved' is the abstract's wording; it is activity, not a dopamine measurement.

claim: Anticipation of an abstract reward can result in dopamine release in an anatomical pathway distinct from the one associated with peak pleasure.
excerpt: the anticipation of an abstract reward can result in dopamine release in an anatomical pathway distinct from that associated with the peak pleasure itself.
context: One study. The abstract says 'can result in'; it does not say it always does.
